hook.text: Patients preferred a longer, painful procedure over a shorter one if the ending was less painful.

buildup.text: Kahneman found we judge experiences by their peak moment and how they end, not by total duration.

discovery.text: This is the peak-end rule. A great finale rewrites how the whole experience felt in memory.

twist.text: Duration neglect means a 20-minute bad meeting and a 60-minute one feel equally bad if the peak matches.

climax.text: Restaurants serve great desserts for this reason. The ending shapes the whole recalled experience.

punchline.text: End well; they'll remember it well.

quiz.question: What two moments define how we remember an experience?
options: The peak moment and the ending

details.summary: The peak-end rule describes how people evaluate experiences primarily by their most intense moment and their ending, rather than by the total amount of pleasure or pain. A vacation with a terrible final day is remembered worse than a shorter but smoothly ending trip.
details.whyItMatters: The peak-end rule explains why endings and highlights matter disproportionately. Businesses, healthcare providers, and experience designers who manage peak moments and endings can dramatically improve customer satisfaction and memory.
takeaways: Experiences are judged mainly by their peak intensity and how they ended
Duration of the experience has surprisingly little effect on memory evaluation
Improving the ending can transform the remembered quality of any experience

faq.question: What is the most famous demonstration of the peak-end rule?
faq.answer: Kahneman's cold water experiment showed that people preferred a longer painful experience that ended with slightly warmer water over a shorter but uniformly cold one. The better ending made the objectively worse experience feel preferable.

faq.question: How can businesses use the peak-end rule?
faq.answer: Ensure the customer experience ends on a high note: a warm goodbye, a parting gift, or a smooth final step. Create deliberate positive peaks during the experience. Duration matters less than these two moments for remembered satisfaction.
